# Play — Leapfrog

- SudokuPad: [Leapfrog on SudokuPad](https://sudokupad.)
- f-puzzles: [Leapfrog on f-puzzles](https://www.f-puzzles.com/?)

Both links carry the same f-puzzles JSON (lz-string compressed), including the solution, so SudokuPad can check your answer.
The frog clue is invented and has no f-puzzles entry. Each lily pad is exported as a **cosmetic** green circle with its total, placed on the
outside position (row 0/10 or column 0/10). The apps won't enforce the rule. That's no problem for solving, because the answer check
compares against the solution. I have not opened the links in a browser, and the pads may not show if an app doesn't draw circles outside the grid.
In that case use `grid.svg` in this folder as the reference picture: 14 pads, read from the side they stand on.

Pads (side, line, total): above c1 10, above c2 14, above c7 13, above c9 14; left of r1 12, left of r7 11; right of r1 16, r3 15, r5 14,
r6 13, r7 16; below c2 15, below c3 10, below c9 16.

Fallback: `puzzle.json` in this folder is the machine-readable source (constraints, solution).
